content.text: Intent

A single, responsive, static HTML page that presents an automotive dealer's brand and models and persuades visitors to request a test drive or a quote. Each request becomes a lead request (a visitor's request for a test drive or a quote, with their contact details) that the dealer's staff review and follow up on. It serves prospective car buyers and the dealer's sales team.
Scope

IN: one static HTML page (HTML + CSS, no framework, no server) with a hero and call to action, featured models, key features, customer testimonials, a lead request form, and contact / dealer location.
IN: a screen where staff keep lead requests (entered by hand through its form).
OUT: delivering the page form's data to the platform or any other system — deferred; the form only validates and confirms on the page for now.
OUT: user accounts, online payment, model inventory or pricing management (model content is fixed text on the page), multi-language support.
Scenarios
None — the page is a single read-then-submit flow; the form's behaviour is carried by R2 and R3.
Requirements

R1: The system SHALL provide one static HTML page containing, in this order, a hero with headline and a call-to-action leading to the lead request form, a featured models section, a key features section, a customer testimonials section, the lead request form, and a contact section with dealer address, phone and opening hours.

R2: WHEN a visitor submits the lead request form with full name, a valid email and a request type (test drive or quote) filled in, the page SHALL show a confirmation message and send the entered data nowhere.
The form's fields are full name, email, phone (optional), request type (required, chosen on the form), preferred model (optional) and message (optional).

R3: IF a visitor submits the form with full name empty, request type not chosen, or an email that is empty or not a valid address, THEN the page SHALL show a message next to each offending field and no confirmation.
R4: WHILE the viewport is between 320 px and 1920 px wide, the system SHALL display the page without horizontal scrolling.
R5: WHEN staff open the Lead requests screen, the system SHALL list lead requests newest first.
Moving a request through new, contacted and closed is the status field of the bean table and needs no requirement of its own.

Dependencies
None — no existing entity or spec covers lead requests (entity catalog checked).
Constraints

Considered, none apply: authorization beyond the platform default, performance, volume, availability, privacy and retention, locale, cost. The page makes no network call, so no data leaves the visitor's browser.
Acceptance criteria

A1 (verifies R1): WHEN the page is opened, the system SHALL show the hero, featured models, key features, testimonials, lead request form and contact sections in that order, the hero's call-to-action scrolling to the form.
A2 (verifies R2): WHEN a form with full name, email "a@b.com" and request type quote is submitted, the page SHALL display a confirmation message and issue no network request.
A3 (verifies R3): WHEN the form is submitted with an empty full name, with no request type chosen, or with the email "abc", the page SHALL show a message beside that field and no confirmation.
A4 (verifies R4): WHEN the page is rendered at 320 px and at 1920 px width, the system SHALL show no horizontal scrollbar.
A5 (verifies R5): WHEN two lead requests created one after the other exist and staff open the Lead requests screen, the system SHALL list the later one first.
